analysis: The supplied diff touches only CHANGELOG.md. It adds a v0.9.20 candidate section (head lines 6-13) that raises the default SSD cache write budget from 750 GB to 4 TB (4,000 decimal GB) per rolling day. It also notes release identity preparation for 0.9.20 with publication pending. The changelog says saved limits and environment overrides still take precedence. No code, enforcement paths or tests were supplied. The write-budget enforcement (persistent root-wide rolling-day ledger, write_rate_limited, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_WRITE_GB_PER_DAY) is described in base lines 94-95 and in the cache storage controls entry (base line 17). The budget is relevant to T-041 (SSD tier, endurance guard) and to ADV-002 abuse through donation-driven wear. Next passes should check the code that sets the default: the ledger, the unit conversion (decimal vs binary GB), the interaction with the 20 GiB free-space reserve, and whether the per-donation gate and novel-versus-repeated write share still bound unauthenticated or unique-prompt writes. They should also check the 0.9.20 version bump and any release identity or registry changes. No other changed security behavior is visible in this batch.

findings.detail: The changelog says the default SSD prefix-cache write budget rises from 750 GB to 4 TB per rolling day. The ledger-enforced budget (see the 2026-09-08 SSD disk policy note and T-041 'endurance' guard) is the control that limits how fast cache donations can wear a provider's SSD. A malicious consumer (ADV-002) can send long unique prompts. Those donations are accepted by the per-donation gate (adoption bound plus the 1,024-token floor), and each one writes encrypted blocks to the provider's SSD. At the new default, a provider can absorb about 4 TB/day of such writes before any limit applies. That accelerates drive wear and I/O contention, and it can degrade or end the provider's availability. T-041 does not state the budget value or treat wear-based DoS as a residual risk. The actual code change is not in the supplied units, so this is a documentation and threat-model gap and the enforcement path was not reviewed. Fix: record the new ceiling and its wear/DoS rationale in T-041 or a dedicated entry. Confirm that the 4 TB default is still overridable downward and that the per-account novel-versus-repeated write-share limits still apply.
findings.title: Default SSD write budget raised about 5x with no threat-model update for consumer-driven wear
